Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple well-defined pulmonary nodules of varying sizes (some approaching 3 cm) that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones, particularly on the right side. This specific radiographic pattern, combined with the absence of calcification, is characteristic of necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis and distinguishes it from the upper-zone predominance of tuberculosis or the uniform distribution of typical sarcoidosis.
